item.title: Epic MegaGrants 2026 (Cycle 2)
item.description:
Organisation: Epic Games

Location: Open worldwide. Epic states that if it can legally make payment to you, you are eligible.

Award: Typical grants range from USD 5,000 to USD 75,000, with some exceptional projects receiving up to USD 150,000. Epic states that recipients continue to own their IP and may publish it however they wish, so this is a grant rather than an investment or equity deal. Grants up to and including USD 25,000 may be paid in a single instalment; larger grants are paid across several instalments tied to continued progress. Funds are for project and team expenses such as development and hiring; hardware purchases or rentals are approved only occasionally, case by case. No application fee.

Duration: Cycle 2 of 2026 runs 29 June to 11 December 2026. Submission window 29 June to 4 September 2026 (closes 23:59 ET), review 5 September to 4 December 2026, notices 7 to 11 December 2026. Cycle 1 ran 12 January to 19 June 2026.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

Epic MegaGrants are financial grants from Epic Games for creative, noteworthy and innovative projects built in and around Unreal Engine, or projects that enhance the open source 3D graphics ecosystem. Over 2,000 grants have been awarded to date. The programme is explicitly aimed at smaller teams, solo developers and individuals as well as studios: Epic states that individuals and small teams are eligible and encouraged, and that it treats every project equally regardless of who you are. WHAT IS FUNDED: (1) INDIE GAMES, small or solo teams working in Unreal Engine, submitted past the idea and design phase with at least some working prototype, ideally with a video link; (2) UEFN EXPERIENCES, Fortnite Creative islands and interactive experiences built in Unreal Editor for Fortnite; (3) ENGINE MIGRATION, a proportion of MegaGrants is reserved for teams moving a partially developed project from another engine to Unreal; (4) FILM, TV AND LIVE EVENTS, including live-action and animated films and shows, broadcast, live and location-based events; (5) OTHER NON-GAMES VERTICALS such as architecture, automotive, manufacturing, simulation, product design, advertising and VR/AR, where more detailed project plans and prototypes are expected; (6) EDUCATION, including research, curricula and course development and university programmes, though for institutions Epic accepts submissions only from degree-granting schools and educators at such schools; (7) TOOLS AND OPEN SOURCE, creating open source tools or enhancing open source software using Unreal Engine. NON-UNREAL PROJECTS ARE ELIGIBLE if you want to move them to Unreal Engine, or if the project enhances open source 3D content creation whether or not it relates to Unreal Engine. EVALUATION rests on three things: quality and unique appeal (high-quality demos or builds, well-documented descriptions, technical ambition); community benefit (how you will give back, for example open-sourcing the project, releasing assets through a marketplace, sharing learnings, or shipping an SDK, tool or plug-in); and viability (a clear budget with major spend areas and a project plan with milestones, deliverables and timeline). NOTE ON DEADLINES: the FAQ still describes MegaGrants as an ongoing programme with no specific deadline, but the timeline published on the same page now runs in fixed cycles, and the Cycle 2 submission window closes 4 September 2026 at 23:59 ET. Treat the cycle date as the operative deadline. You may apply for more than one project, and may reapply for the same project after a decision if you have made updates. Epic is not offering sponsorships and cannot give feedback on applications. Apply at megagrants.unrealengine.com.

item.title: Scuola Piccola Zattere: International Fellowship and Residency 2027 (Venice)
item.description:
Organisation: Scuola Piccola Zattere

Location: Venice, Italy. Open to any nationality.

Award: EUR 5,000 fellowship grant plus a EUR 2,000 research budget, accommodation in Venice, an individual study space within a shared studio, and round-trip travel to Venice. Collectives and duos share a single grant and one accommodation. No application fee.

Duration: Three months, in one of two slots: early January to early April 2027, or mid-April to mid-July 2027. Applicants may name one slot or indicate availability for both.

Deadline: 04 Sep 2026

Scuola Piccola Zattere is an independent non-profit centre for continuous education and research in the expanded field of contemporary arts, running exhibitions, commissions, fellowships, workshops, seminars, performances and public discussions as one connected research ecosystem rather than separate strands. Two international fellowships are offered. The support is unusually solid for a research fellowship: EUR 5,000 as a grant, EUR 2,000 as a research budget, accommodation, travel and a study space for three months. SEASON THEME: the 2026-2027 cycle is titled Living Document, investigating archives, regulatory documents, collective rituals, games, performative instructions, and the relationship between bodies, architecture and social organisation. Fellows join that shared inquiry while continuing their own work, and are expected to keep an active presence in the institution and contribute to public events through workshops, seminars, presentations, screenings or performances. The fellowship overlaps with the run-up to and opening of the 2027 Architecture Biennale, which is a real advantage if your research benefits from that traffic. ELIGIBILITY: artists, curators, researchers, architects, choreographers, performers and writers of any nationality, as individuals, collectives or duos. Good English is required, and non-EU applicants need a valid passport for international travel. No age limit, but the organisers say it is especially intended for practitioners in the post-academic stage of their career, typically under 40. You must be prepared to spend the full period in Venice, so this is not a remote or partial-attendance fellowship. WHAT THEY WANT: an active research process that can develop through discussion and experimentation, tied to the Living Document theme, not a finished stand-alone project proposal. The motivation letter, portfolio and public programming proposal are read as one integrated application. Deadline 4 September 2026 at 10:00 CEST.

item.title: Open Call 2026/2027 'Where is the tomorrow we saw yesterday?' (spazioSERRA)
item.description:
Organisation: spazioSERRA

Location: Milan, Italy. spazioSERRA operates inside the Milano Lancetti passante railway station; registered office Via Maloia 1, 20158 Milan. Open to artists and collectives of any nationality, aged 18 or over.

Award: EUR 500 to EUR 2,000 financial contribution per selected project, set according to the project's characteristics and available resources, paid at the end of the collaboration against documented expenses with traceable payment methods. No cost to the artist for use of the exhibition space or for the work of the spazioSERRA team. Application fee: EUR 12 membership fee per person (multiplied by the number of members for collectives).

Duration: Collaborations developed across the 2027 exhibition and project season

Deadline: 06 Sep 2026

spazioSERRA turns ten in 2027, and this open call is framed as a deliberate break from how independent art usually asks artists to arrive: with deadlines met, ideas already defined, and a project ready to be exhibited. The call asks 'where is the tomorrow we saw yesterday?' and states plainly that it is not looking for completed projects or stabilised visions, but for practices, processes, obsessions and still-open questions. Site-specific installations, performances, editorial productions, videos, urban interventions, hybrid collaborations and forms that are still undefined are all welcome; the point is not the format but the urgency running through it, and the willingness to enter a shared research process that can slow down, change direction and stay incomplete long enough to transform. WHAT IT LEADS TO: the call identifies artists, collectives and research practices with whom spazioSERRA may develop collaborations during the 2027 exhibition and project season, which may take the form of solo or group exhibitions, site-specific installations, performances, editorial productions, video projects, collaborations with institutions or external organisations, and further projects developed together. If selected, the artist or collective begins a curatorial dialogue with spazioSERRA aimed at developing an exhibition and/or additional projects, jointly defined during the collaboration. FUNDING: each selected project receives a financial contribution of EUR 500 to EUR 2,000, determined by the project's characteristics and available resources, covering production costs of the work (which remains the property of the artist or collective), travel, food and accommodation, and communication and promotion materials. The contribution is paid at the end of the collaboration unless otherwise agreed, and spazioSERRA reimburses only documented expenses paid by traceable methods with the relevant tax documentation. It is explicitly a contribution towards the realisation of the project and/or the practice, not necessarily full coverage of production costs; if the project is developed with external partners bringing additional resources, the budget may be supplemented by mutual agreement. Use of the exhibition space and the work of the spazioSERRA team cost the artist nothing. SELECTION: no exhibition project or defined proposal is required; the jury assesses the artistic research as a whole, including the applicant's path, the languages used, the questions explored, the potential for development and compatibility with spazioSERRA's curatorial vision. The selecting curatorial collective is Pietro Agostini, Lidia Barca, Tracy Bassil, Virginia Dal Magro, Massimiliano Fanto, Camilla Gurgone, Giulia Maffioli Brigatti, Cristiano Rizzo, Victoria Tincati and Valentina Toccaceli. First selection in November 2026, interviews November to December 2026, final notification by December 2026. APPLICATION: online form open 15 July to 6 September 2026, with a single PDF containing statement, artistic CV and a selection of works, shared via a stable online link viewable without download, authorisation or password; collectives list all members. FEE: EUR 12 membership fee per person, multiplied by the number of members for a collective. Contact: info.spazioserra@gmail.com.

item.title: Utrecht University: PhD, Media and Democracy in the 1970s (NWO Vidi project)
item.description:
Organisation: Utrecht University, Faculty of Humanities, Department of History and Art History

Location: Utrecht, Netherlands (Drift 6)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 36 to 40 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 18-month initial contract, extended to four years after a positive first-year assessment

Deadline: 06 Sep 2026

Fully funded PhD position in the NWO-funded Vidi project 'Democracy and the (de-)regulation of the media in Europe since the 1970s', which reads the contestation and transformation of democracy in the last quarter of the twentieth century through media governance. This sub-project examines how social movements, pirate broadcasters and alternative media initiatives challenged the public broadcasting monopoly across Western Europe during the long 1970s, drawing on archival research. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in history or a related field, a demonstrated interest in the history of democracy and media governance, professional English plus at least one other European language, archival research experience and a collaborative approach. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy number 5535). Project leader Dr Pepijn Corduwener (p.corduwener@uu.nl). Deadline 6 September 2026.

item.title: Edward F. Albee Foundation: William Flanagan Memorial Creative Persons Center Residency (Winter/Spring 2027)
item.description:
Organisation: The Edward F. Albee Foundation

Location: Montauk, Long Island, New York, USA (about two miles from downtown Montauk and the Atlantic)

Award: Fully funded residency: private en-suite bedroom and separate working studio, USD 2,500 stipend for domestic Fellows paid on successful completion, or reimbursement of expenses capped at USD 2,500 for international Fellows. No application fee and no residency fee.

Duration: One full calendar month between January and June 2027; partial months are not offered

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

Edward Albee founded this foundation in 1962 with the proceeds from Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?, and it has run The Barn in Montauk for close to sixty years as a place for writers and visual artists to get uninterrupted time. The house sits on a secluded knoll and takes four residents at a time, usually two writers and two visual artists, each with an en-suite bedroom and a separate studio. The environment is deliberately simple and communal: residents share responsibility for the space and are expected to work seriously and keep it quiet for everyone else. ELIGIBILITY: any creative person over 18, any nationality, students included; selection uses talent and need as the only criteria. There are no fees at all, to apply or to stay. Domestic Fellows get a USD 2,500 stipend on completing the residency; international Fellows get expenses reimbursed up to USD 2,500. DATES: this cycle covers residencies from January to June 2027. Applications open at 08:00 on 17 August 2026 and close on 14 September 2026, through apply.albeefoundation.org. The next cycle (July-November 2027) opens 11 January 2027 and closes 15 February 2027. The Barn is closed every December. Contact apply@albeefoundation.org or (212) 226-2020.

item.title: Normsy: Social Media Measurement Methods Incubator RFP
item.description:
Organisation: Normsy (a project of Civic Health Project)

Location: Remote. Open to individuals and teams from academic, academic-adjacent and industry backgrounds; no stated country restriction. Research context is X/Twitter (proposals may be multi-platform but must include X).

Award: USD 1,000 awarded to each of the top 5 proposals, plus up to USD 20,000 to fund R&D and/or testing with one selected partner individual or team. Preference for budgets where at least 50 percent goes to research costs (survey respondents, LLM or X API credits). No application fee.

Duration: Proposals must set out concrete deliverables within 6 months of starting; the partnership is framed as the start of a potentially longer-term collaboration

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

Normsy, a project of Civic Health Project, runs a small methods incubator for new strategies to measure or estimate the impact of prosocial social-media interventions. Normsy identifies toxic posts (typically content attacking or violating civic norms) and offers real users a set of AI-generated prosocial comments to choose from and post; the open question is how to estimate the effect of those comments on content producers, other commenters and bystanders who consume content without interacting measurably. The current approach combines survey experiments (how active X users respond emotionally to threads with and without the intervention, and how it shifts agreement with and support for the original post) with paid X API platform data (classifying comments before and after an intervention, plus coarse engagement metrics that cost money each time they are recollected). WHAT THEY WANT: a systematic way to leverage available platform data and maximise the utility of the survey experiments. Example proposals include a strategy for measuring toxicity/prosociality and reach/visibility of a thread over time with a randomisation design generating a control group of threads, or an approach to benchmarking the prosocial potential of AI-generated comments through an iterative arena with human judges or a theory-backed LLM validation approach with human validation. The brief is explicit that methodological innovation, causal identification, scalable measurement frameworks and novel observational approaches matter far more than proposing new intervention types; proposals need not study Normsy exclusively but must explain how the evaluation design transfers to it. Ethics and IRB considerations are central and Normsy will collaborate with selected researchers on ethics review and implementation planning. Researchers retain publication independence and IP; the partnership is expected to produce data for an academic paper. SUBMIT: one zipped folder through the linked Google Form containing a 3-page proposal (design, work already done, work still needed to scale and implement), a budget document for the USD 20,000, a timeline with concrete deliverables inside 6 months, and short bios for all team members. Award notifications mid-October 2026. Questions to kylan@civichealthproject.org; informal and exploratory conversations welcome.

item.title: Connect and Create: Circulation of Performing Arts and Music (Africa-Europe) - 2nd Call
item.description:
Organisation: Goethe-Institut and Expertise France, in collaboration with Institut francais (Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture consortium)

Location: Applicants based in one of the 47 eligible sub-Saharan African countries (Kenya included) or one of the 27 EU Member States. Touring in Africa and/or Europe.

Award: EUR 15,000 to EUR 39,500 per project, covering travel, visas, insurance, accommodation, per diems, local transport and shipping of scenographic and technical elements. No application fee.

Duration: Projects carried out between February and December 2027

Deadline: 30 Sep 2026

The Circulation strand of Connect and Create funds the touring and dissemination of African artistic creations across Africa and Europe. It is part of the Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture programme (EUR 8M, led by the Goethe-Institut and Expertise France in partnership with Institut francais, supported by the European Union), and is a different strand from the Professional Mobilities call also on the desk. THIS CARD IS THE SECOND CALL, deadline 30 September 2026 (the first call closed 30 November 2025). AMOUNT: EUR 15,000 to EUR 39,500 per project. WHAT IS FUNDED: mobility costs for artistic teams, including transport, visas, insurance, lodging, per diems, local transport, and shipping of scenographic and technical elements. WHO CAN APPLY: artistic teams (performing arts companies, music ensembles, collectives) based in sub-Saharan Africa; dissemination structures (production houses, artist managers, theatres, labels, venues) based in Africa or Europe; and event organisers (festivals, markets, professional gatherings) in Africa or Europe. Applicants must be legally established in one of the 47 eligible sub-Saharan African countries, Kenya among them, or one of the 27 EU Member States. INDIVIDUALS CANNOT APPLY. ELIGIBLE PROJECTS, two formats: (1) TOURS, requiring a minimum of 5 pre-booked dates across at least 3 different African countries, or at least 3 pre-booked dates in one or more European countries; (2) PROGRAMMING WITHIN MAJOR EVENTS, requiring a festival, market or professional gathering in Africa or Europe to host at least 3 artistic teams from different African countries. TIMELINE: activities must take place between February and December 2027; selection committee December 2026, results announced January 2027. PRIORITY is given to projects that build on existing tandems already collaborating, feature emerging artists, use eco-responsible practices, and address inclusion. APPLY via the Institut francais emundus portal. Questions: connectandcreate@expertisefrance.fr.

item.title: Arts Council England: Music Growth Fund, GBP 40,001-100,000 strand
item.description:
Organisation: Arts Council England

Location: England. Supports new music by living, UK-based artists and music creators.

Award: GBP 40,001 to GBP 100,000, from a total annual budget of GBP 2,000,000 for this strand in 2026/27. You must find at least 50 percent of the total project budget as CASH match funding, and upload a completed finance template alongside your most recent financial statement (sole traders may provide the finance template only). No application fee.

Duration: Two rounds across 2026/27; the next closes 1 October 2026

Deadline: 01 Oct 2026

The Music Growth Fund is Arts Council England's new investment programme for growth in new music, meaning original live performance, sound recording or musical work recently or newly created or performed by living UK-based artists and music creators. It sits inside the wider GBP 45 million Music Growth Package. WHO IT IS FOR: music festivals, music managers, music promoters, music publishers, record labels, recording studios, rehearsal spaces and grassroots music venues, plus established sector bodies and other sector support organisations that support them. Each applicant type has its own Applicant Specific Guidance on the Music Growth Package pages. IMPORTANT: this is business and organisational investment, not a grant for individual artists to make work. Individual artists, bands, producers and artist collectives should instead look at the separate Music Creators Growth Fund (GBP 10,000-20,000), whose guidance lands 1 September 2026 with the portal opening 1 October 2026. WHAT TO PROPOSE: how investment will be used to grow music businesses and/or the wider music industry, and enhance opportunities for artists and music creators, industry professionals, music fans and new audiences. Growth can mean increased reach, stronger business models, improved sustainability, skills development or expanded capacity, and is judged in the context of each applicant's own scale and ambitions. DECISION CRITERIA: potential for growth, effective use of funds, contribution to a fairer and more inclusive music industry, and contribution to a climate resilient music industry. BEFORE YOU START: you need an approved profile on the Arts Council grants management system before you can submit, so allow time for that. Arts Council reserves the right to change the programme, so check you are on the latest guidance. THIS STRAND: GBP 40,001 to GBP 100,000, with a GBP 2,000,000 annual budget for 2026/27 and a 50 percent cash match requirement, which is the main thing that will decide whether this strand is realistic for you. You must also upload a completed finance template as well as your most recent financial statement; sole traders may submit the finance template alone. ROUNDS FOR 2026/27 (GBP 1,000-40,000 strand): Round 1 opens 6 August and closes 3 September 2026, decision 28 October. Round 2 opens 4 September and closes 15 October 2026, decision 28 October. Round 3 opens 16 October and closes 26 November 2026, decision 3 February 2027. Round 4 opens 27 November 2026 and closes 7 January 2027, decision 9 March 2027. ROUNDS FOR THE GBP 40,001-100,000 strand: Round 1 opens 7 September and closes 1 October 2026, decision 30 November. Round 2 opens 23 November 2026 and closes 15 January 2027, decision 8 March 2027.

item.title: Artist Grant: Unrestricted $1,200 Visual Artist Grant (November 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Artist Grant

Location: Remote (worldwide). No residency or travel component.

Award: Unrestricted USD 1,200 grant to one visual artist per round, awarded three times a year. Application fee of USD 30, paid separately via Stripe or PayPal.

Duration: One-off unrestricted award; no reporting or project period

Deadline: 15 Nov 2026

Artist Grant awards an unrestricted USD 1,200 grant to one visual artist three times a year, on a deliberately low-friction application: NO grant proposal is required. You email a link to your website, or 3-5 images of your work as JPG, PNG or PDF, plus a resume, CV or short bio with your name, to submit@artistgrant.org, and separately pay the USD 30 fee through Stripe or PayPal. If the name on your payment differs from the name on your email, say so in the email. ELIGIBILITY: visual artists aged 18 or over, worldwide. Past winners may NOT apply again. MEDIA ACCEPTED: painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, photography, mixed media, installation, and new or alternative visual art forms. NOT ACCEPTED: film and video, music, theatre, dance. SELECTION CRITERIA: a cohesive body of work; well-crafted work; well-presented work, judged with an explicit allowance that artists have differing financial means for presentation; work that communicates its viewpoint, ideas and concepts clearly, effectively and creatively; and work that is not derivative. RESULTS: all applicants are notified within 6-8 weeks of each deadline, and results are announced on the website, social media and newsletter. They will not respond to individual queries during the review period. VISIBILITY: grantees are showcased on the website, social media and marketing materials, and selected applicants are featured on social media with permission. Artists retain their copyrights. NOTE: the grant recurs on 15 March, 15 July and 15 November each year, and this desk lists each round separately. There is a USD 30 application fee.

item.title: transmediale x DARC: Interstices, Research (in) the Gaps, PhD/Research Workshop
item.description:
Organisation: Digital Aesthetics Research Center (DARC), Aarhus University, in collaboration with transmediale

Location: Berlin, Germany; the workshop runs alongside transmediale 2027 (festival 26 to 31 January 2027). Open to researchers based anywhere, inside or outside the academy.

Award: No submission fee. The published call does not state a participation fee, honorarium, travel or accommodation support, so confirm with the organisers before budgeting. Accepted participants present a paper at the workshop and their condensed text is distributed as a newspaper-style article at the festival.

Duration: Research workshop held around transmediale 2027 in Berlin (festival 26 to 31 January 2027)

Deadline: Closed 28 Aug 2026

The annual DARC PhD/Research Workshop, organised by the Digital Aesthetics Research Center at Aarhus University with transmediale, responds to transmediale's 2027 thematic framework. THEME: 'Interstices: Research (in) the gaps'. An interstice is the small space between objects set closely together, the cords in a rope or the atoms in a crystal lattice: an emptiness produced by the structure it belongs to, and without which that structure could not be what it is. In crystallography, interstitial sites are the spaces a lattice and its basis generate but do not fill, and interstitial diffusion, the movement of small atoms through the gaps of a host lattice, is the mechanism by which materials transform. The call asks what the equivalent sites are in social, cultural and computational structures: where are the gaps these combinations generate but do not fill, what moves through them, and do they carry transformative power? It works through Yancey Strickler's dark forest theory of the internet (the withdrawal of meaningful exchange from the open, surveilled, indexed web into private channels), the Dark Forest Collective's anthology and its 'cozyweb' of small sheltered spaces, dark nets, miniverses and moving castles as interstitial spaces produced by and defined against the dominant web, and Bogna Konior's extension of the dark forest metaphor to the opacity of AI systems, where silence is refusal rather than absence and the forest is increasingly inhabited by other-than-human intelligences that opt out of engagement with people. Where big tech pursues efficiency through the automation of human perception, cognition, identification and aesthetics, artists and researchers explore the non/more-than-human, glitchy, noisy, machinic, datafied and dark to build new expression and critique of data-ism and what is marketed as artificial intelligence, including the dangers and potentials inside badly curated data models, between polluting data centres, and in skeuomorphic interfaces. WHAT THEY WANT: proposals from artists, researchers and practitioners for work that occupies and moves through gaps that are social as well as structural, ontological and material. The gaps are physical too: the heat of data centres and their thirst for water, latency in the cables, unindexed nodes. The call invites speculations, practical interventions and inferences that fill the gaps and expand the diversity of possible communications and communities that can inhabit dark forests, including those built on, against and beneath the infrastructures underlying them, and welcomes work on the (dis-)continuous histories of technological exploration of computational infrastructures over the last 30 years or longer, and on how current artistic, theoretical and technical explorations repeat or break from them. WHO: PhD candidates and early-career researchers, with submissions welcome from researchers inside and outside the academy, including artists, designers and curators. PARTICIPANT EXPECTATIONS: participants write a paper and present it at the workshop, and on the basis of that peer review shorten the research into a newspaper-length article for distribution at the transmediale festival. item.description:
Organisation: Liveline, delivered by Music Venue Trust with Save Our Scene and the Association of Independent Promoters

Location: United Kingdom. Guarantorship shows must be at Music Venue Alliance member venues; for a full tour at least 70 percent of dates must be at subscribed MVT venues. Regional focus includes the Highlands and Islands, West Wales and Northern Ireland.

Award: No fixed grant sizes published; every application is assessed case by case against a real budget rather than first come first served. The Guarantorship Scheme covers up to 80 percent of losses on a show or tour: if it breaks even nothing is paid, and if it turns a profit the promoter or venue keeps it. The other three funds cover venue hire, travel, accommodation, ferry and remote-access costs, or genre-specific safety, licensing and access costs. No application fee.

Duration: Round 1; applications close Tuesday 18 August 2026

Deadline: Closed 18 Aug 2026

Liveline is a national risk-sharing fund rebuilding grassroots touring, programming and local music scenes across the UK, delivered by Music Venue Trust with Save Our Scene and the Association of Independent Promoters, alongside the LIVE Trust and the industry's voluntary levy on stadium and arena tickets. The premise is that good shows are not happening because the downside risk is too high, so rather than a traditional subsidy it is an incentive-led model that only pays out when things go wrong. FOUR FUNDS: (1) GUARANTORSHIP SCHEME covers up to 80 percent of losses on an individual show or tour, for promoters, in-house bookers, artists or their representatives; break even and nothing is paid, turn a profit and you keep it. (2) LOCAL SCENE DEVELOPMENT FUND covers venue hire costs and local promoter training to build regular programming, for independent promoters or venues developing an in-house programme. (3) TOUR EXTENSION AND REGIONAL ACCESS FUND covers the long travel, fuel, accommodation and ferry costs that stop tours reaching remote parts of the UK, for promoters, agents, management and artists. (4) GENRE SPECIFIC SAFETY AND ACCESS FUND covers extra security, licensing and structural costs for genres and scenes that face additional barriers, for venues, promoters, artists or collectives. ELIGIBILITY: grassroots venues (Music Venue Alliance member venues), independent promoters including AIP members, in-house venue programmers, and artists, agents and teams building sustainable tours. Guarantorship shows must be at MVA subscribed venues, and for a full tour at least 70 percent of dates must be at subscribed MVT venues. TWO CATCHES WORTH KNOWING: tours must NOT already be announced, and Liveline funds a headline artist only once. Applications for Round 1 close Tuesday 18 August 2026. item.title: Transfyr AI Fellowship 2026-2027 (Boston/Cambridge)
item.description:
Organisation: Transfyr

Location: Boston/Cambridge, Massachusetts, US, full-time in person. Remote considered by exception when the project and candidate make it workable.

Award: $125,000 annual compensation plus benefits, plus access to compute, GPUs, data and project support. Applicants are asked to specify the compute, GPU, data or support their project would need. No application fee.

Duration: Full-time for 12 months

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

A one-year, full-time research fellowship for graduate students, recent PhDs and postdocs to lead a project on frontier machine learning problems grounded in how scientific work actually happens. THE PREMISE: Transfyr argues science is missing an observability layer. Lab work is full of tacit decisions, failed attempts, operator judgment, noisy instruments and context that never reaches the written protocol, and the company is building what it calls the world's largest multimodal dataset of scientific execution for models to reason over. Fellows get to work with that data. RESEARCH AGENDA, eight named directions: multimodal reasoning (aligning video, audio, protocol text, instrument traces, timestamps, gaze and outcomes); conflicting evidence (uncertainty and calibration, evidence attribution, contradiction-aware reasoning); long-context scientific memory (long-horizon state tracking, retrieval over process histories, failure and deviation memory); real-world evaluations (benchmark design, process-level metrics, lab-grounded model assessment); tacit expertise (expert-novice comparison, skill representation, human-in-the-loop feedback); physical-world AI (embodied data pipelines, transfer across settings, policy and assistance evaluation); biosecurity and bio-risk observability (synthesis-to-execution verification, emergent capability tracking, autonomous vulnerability detection); and scientific execution ontology (wet-lab-grounded metadata design, cross-domain causal attribution, multi-scale variability mapping). WHAT FELLOWS DO: define a research question, build prototypes, analyse real multimodal scientific-execution data, pressure-test evaluation ideas, and produce a publishable or demo-grade artifact, with direct mentorship from Transfyr's founders, technical team and advisor network across AI, biology, robotics and scientific operations. WHO CAN APPLY: current graduate students able to take leave (and to self-certify that they can commit full-time), recent PhDs and postdocs in machine learning, computer science, computational biology, robotics, human-computer interaction, statistics or adjacent fields. Strong ML fundamentals and evidence of research taste are the bar; the call asks for comfort with ambiguity and curiosity about how science happens in physical environments. International applicants are welcome and visa support is available for selected fellows. IP TERMS, worth reading before applying: Transfyr owns the fellowship work product and supports publication subject to confidentiality and IP review. This is a company fellowship, not an academic one. APPLICATION: a one-page application sent to ai_fellowship@transfyr.ai saying what you want to work on and what resources you need, with links that make your work easy to evaluate; references are requested of finalists. DEADLINE: applications are reviewed on a ROLLING basis; apply by 15 August 2026 for full consideration, decisions roll through late August 2026, fellowship begins around September 2026.
